w:r.w:t: Reference Documentation — How Scores Are Calculated & What They Mean
Every team member receives one Total KPI Score per month. Where that score lands determines the performance rating and outcome below:
High volume of work, excellent quality & collaboration, perfect or near-perfect delivery, strong R&D contribution.
KPI bonus earned + recognition + merit increase consideration.
Strong effort volume, very good to excellent quality/collaboration, consistently on-time, some R&D contribution.
Solid, dependable output typical of real production pace — occasional revision rounds or dependency delays included. Good quality/collaboration, mostly on-time delivery.
Standard compensation. No bonus, no concern.
Below-target volume, and/or quality or collaboration issues, and/or repeated late deliveries.
Low output combined with quality, collaboration, or delivery problems.

KPI Bonus Threshold: A score of 55 or higher earns the monthly KPI bonus (Good or Great tier). These ranges are calibrated to realistic animation production pace — mostly on-time with some revision cycles and dependency delays — not to an idealized, friction-free month.
Total KPI Score = ( Total Effort Points × Quality Multiplier × Collaboration Multiplier ) + Total Delivery Points + R&D Bonus
Each component of that formula is built from data already tracked in Asana (Anim8 Production Pipeline → Anim8 KPI) plus two manager assessments made once per month:
Every completed task carries an effort value based on its Effort field: S = 1 pt, M = 2 pts, L = 4 pts, XL = 8 pts. All completed tasks for the month are summed into 'Total Effort Points.'
Manager sets a monthly Quality Rating (1–5). This converts to Quality Points (10/9/8/6/4) via automation rules, then to a multiplier of Quality Points ÷ 10.
Manager sets a monthly Collaboration Rating (1–5), same conversion as Quality: Points (10/9/8/6/4) ÷ 10.

Every task gets a Delivery Status. Rules auto-assign points: On-Time/Early = +2, 1–2 Days Late = -1, 3–5 Days Late = -2, 1 Week Late = -4, Weeks/Months Late = -8. Summed across the month = 'Total Delivery Points.'
Manager sets a monthly R&D Contribution rating: 3 = Major Innovation (+15), 2 = Good Learning (+10), 1 = Some Learning (+5), 0 = None (+0).
Effort Points — pulled from each task's Effort field (S/M/L/XL) via automation rule.
Delivery Points — pulled from each task's Delivery Status field via automation rule, summed for the month on the Dashboard.
Manual, once per month (on the person's KPI Summary task)
Quality Rating (1–5) — set by the manager, based on revisions needed and overall craft.
Collaboration Rating (1–5) — set by the manager, based on teamwork, responsiveness, communication.
R&D Contribution (0–3) — set by the manager, based on whether the person's work this month contributed new learning, techniques, or innovation to the studio.

5. Weighted Scale for Part-Time & Contract Staff

The performance bands and formula above assume a full-time, 40-hour work week. Applied as-is, a part-time or contract team member would need to work proportionally harder just to reach the same tier as a full-time employee — not because their work is worse, but because they simply have fewer hours to generate Effort and Delivery Points. To keep the same bands fair for everyone, the volume-driven parts of the formula are normalized by an FTE Ratio.
Set once per person (only updated if contracted hours change):

Effort Points and Delivery Points are divided by the person's FTE Ratio before entering the score. Quality, Collaboration, and R&D are left untouched — these measure how well someone works, not how much, so they apply the same to everyone regardless of schedule.
Total KPI Score = ( [Total Effort Points ÷ FTE Ratio] × Quality Multiplier × Collaboration Multiplier ) + [Total Delivery Points ÷ FTE Ratio] + R&D Bonus

Without normalization, this person's month reads as Bad purely because of fewer contracted hours — not performance. Normalized, they land at Average: the same tier a full-time employee doing the equivalent proportional output would land in. Normalization doesn't inflate or deflate the bar for anyone; it just re-bases volume to what a full 40-hour week would produce.
1. Work is completed in Anim8 Production Pipeline; Delivery Status and Effort are set per task.
2. Completed/archived tasks move into Anim8 KPI, organized by month.
3. At month-end, the Dashboard is checked for Total Effort Points and Total Delivery Points per person.
4. A KPI Summary task is created per person; Quality, Collaboration, and R&D ratings are selected.
5. The Total KPI Score formula calculates automatically and determines the performance band.
6. Scores are reviewed 1-on-1 with each team member, then archived quarterly to Anim8 ARCHIVES.
